bibliography.abstract: Origin-destination (OD) matrices sit behind much of quantitative transport planning, from model calibration and accessibility analysis to the appraisal of new services and development. The increasing emphasis on place-based solutions requires mobility data that can support decision-making not only at the strategic level, but also at finer spatial scales. This requires up-to-date OD evidence at small-area resolution, disaggregated by travel mode and purpose, which remains either inaccessible or unavailable. In this work, we present dense MSOA-to-MSOA OD matrices for England and Wales, segmented by seven travel modes and representative time periods, with eight trip purposes for the weekday morning peak. The matrices are built by calibrating aggregate mobile network data provided by BT against National Travel Survey (NTS), census and trip-rate evidence, preserving the observed spatial structure of movement while referencing its age, mode and purpose composition to the survey. The open-source data processing pipeline is released alongside the matrices, so that the construction of the dataset can be inspected in full and adapted to other years, regions or assumptions.
bibliography.comment: 13 pages, 1 figure, 3 tables. Supplementary material provided as an ancillary file
bibliography.title: Travel Mode- and Purpose-Specific Origin-Destination Matrices for England and Wales from Fused Travel Survey and Mobile Network Data

en.caveats: The trip purpose and mode segmentations rely on calibrating mobile network signals against travel surveys, meaning the fine-grained classifications are modeled estimates rather than directly observed behaviors.
en.what: The researchers generated dense Middle Layer Super Output Area (MSOA) to MSOA origin-destination matrices for England and Wales, segmented by seven travel modes and eight trip purposes for the weekday morning peak. The dataset was constructed by calibrating aggregate mobile network data from BT against the National Travel Survey, census data, and trip-rate evidence to preserve spatial movement structures while aligning demographics and travel purposes.
en.why: It provides planners with highly disaggregated, small-area mobility data that was previously inaccessible, enabling more precise place-based transport modeling and accessibility analysis.
